suggestions.reason: Significant run-validity concern, not covered by any assertion: the transcript's Step 2 shows the executor deliberately reading eval_metadata.json — which lists all four expectations verbatim — before doing any work, and explicitly says 'this confirmed the plan below before writing anything.' That means this run isn't a blind test of whether the skill-distiller skill alone produces expectation-satisfying output; the executor had direct sight of the grading criteria and could (consciously or not) optimize straight at them. This weakens the eval's power to attribute the clean pass to the skill's guidance versus the model simply satisfying known test criteria. Worth either removing eval_metadata.json from the executor's visible working directory during real runs, or treating any run where the executor admits to reading it as a contaminated/non-blind sample.

The eval prompt says 'Distill a skill from this source: a raw Slack thread transcript...' but no such transcript exists as an input fixture in the eval directory — the executor had to invent it (outputs/raw-slack-transcript.md) before distilling it. That means the same model authors both the material to be distilled and its distillation, and controls how cleanly the raw material converges on the target rule and how many/which incident-style references it contains. A fixed, pre-authored synthetic transcript fixture (checked into the eval directory) would make the eval a more faithful, reproducible test of distillation skill specifically, decoupled from the model's separate skill at inventing plausible incident narratives.

eval_feedback.overall: All four expectations pass with strong, independently-reproduced evidence (re-ran lint_skill.py myself rather than trusting the transcript). The assertions themselves are reasonably discriminating — they require an actual clean distillation and an actual firing lint result with real numbers, not just filename/existence checks. The main weakness isn't the assertions but the run setup: the executor saw the eval's own expectations file mid-task (a blind-test validity issue) and had to self-author the raw source material it was graded on distilling (reducing how cleanly this isolates distillation skill from narrative-authoring skill). Both are flagged above as suggestions rather than assertion failures, since the produced output genuinely and substantively satisfies what was asked.
